title: Why Inflation Doesn’t Affect Us All the Same

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《DealBook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的DealBook峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的人物，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk,
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、

sentences.en: Christine Lagarde, Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼等许多人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话实况。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在nytimes.com上直播部分采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》

sentences.en: Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容一个月的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: The numbers, please.
sentences.zh: 请报一下数据。

sentences.en: And here they are, our consumer price index for the month of April, headline, up 8.3 percent.
sentences.zh: 数据来了，我们4月份的消费者价格指数，总体上涨了8.3%。

sentences.en: On Wednesday, new numbers from the U.S.
sentences.zh: 周三，来自美国

sentences.en: government showed that inflation is still climbing at a rapid pace.
sentences.zh: 政府的最新数据显示，通货膨胀仍在快速攀升。

sentences.en: Let me give you some context, guys.
sentences.zh: 各位，让我来提供一些背景信息。

sentences.en: A year ago, if you go back to this headline number, we're at 8.3 percent for April.
sentences.zh: 一年前，如果回顾这个总体数据，我们4月份是8.3%。

sentences.en: A year ago, we were at 4.2 percent.
sentences.zh: 而一年前，我们是4.2%。

sentences.en: We have doubled these numbers over the last year.
sentences.zh: 过去一年里，这些数字翻了一番。

sentences.en: And President Biden has now declared war on rising consumer prices.
sentences.zh: 拜登总统现在已经向不断上涨的消费价格宣战了。

sentences.en: I want every American to know that I'm taking inflation very seriously and it's my top domestic priority.
sentences.zh: 我想让每一位美国人都知道，我非常重视通货膨胀，这是我国内工作的首要任务。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague, economics reporter Ben
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事，经济记者本·

sentences.en: Castleman, on how inflation is likely to actually affect you depending on where you are in life.
sentences.zh: 卡斯尔曼，将探讨通货膨胀如何根据你所处的人生阶段对你产生实际影响。

sentences.en: It's Thursday, May 12th.
sentences.zh: 今天是5月12日，星期四。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the show.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到节目。

sentences.en: Thanks for being in the studio.
sentences.zh: 感谢来到演播室。

sentences.en: Thanks for coming in the office.
sentences.zh: 感谢来到办公室。

sentences.en: We appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们很感激。

sentences.en: The pizza may have played a role.
sentences.zh: 披萨可能起了一定作用。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday.
sentences.zh: 今天是周三。

sentences.en: It's pizza.
sentences.zh: 是披萨日。

sentences.en: Free pizza day.
sentences.zh: 免费披萨日。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's not about us.
sentences.zh: 重点不是我们。

sentences.en: It's about the pizza.
sentences.zh: 重点是披萨。

sentences.en: You said it, not me.
sentences.zh: 这话是你说的，不是我说的。

sentences.en: So we want to talk to you, surprise, surprise, about inflation, which remains the dominant story of the U.S.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们要和你聊聊——不出所料——关于通货膨胀的话题，它目前仍是美国经济的主导性议题。

sentences.en: economy right now.
sentences.zh: 经济现在的情况。

sentences.en: And I want to start by asking you about this inflation calculator that I know you helped create.
sentences.zh: 我想先问问你关于这个通胀计算器的问题，我知道是你参与创建的。

sentences.en: What is the idea behind it?
sentences.zh: 它背后的理念是什么？

sentences.en: Well, so inflation right now, as we all know, is running at the fastest rate in decades.
sentences.zh: 嗯，正如我们所知，目前的通胀率处于几十年来最快的水平。

sentences.en: And the reality is that your inflation experience and my inflation experience and my mom's inflation experience are going to be different based on where we live
sentences.zh: 现实情况是，你、我和我母亲对通胀的感受会因为我们居住的地方

sentences.en: and how we spend our money and how we live our lives.
sentences.zh: 以及我们如何消费、如何生活而有所不同。

sentences.en: And so what we set out to do was to illustrate that a little bit and to give people a way of understanding the inflation they're feeling and
sentences.zh: 所以我们着手做这件事，是为了说明这一点，让人们能够理解他们所感受到的通胀，

sentences.en: to get a little bit of a real picture of that, but then also to give people a sense of how those
sentences.zh: 并获得一个真实的写照，同时也让人们了解这些

sentences.en: different experiences can really drive how they're experiencing inflation in different ways.
sentences.zh: 不同的经历是如何真正导致他们以不同方式感受通胀的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And just to explain exactly what this inflation calculator actually is, it's a kind of quiz with a short series of questions.
sentences.zh: 为了准确解释这个通胀计算器到底是什么，它其实是一个包含一系列简短问题的小测验。

sentences.en: And once you answer these questions, voila, you get an actual number.
sentences.zh: 当你回答完这些问题后，瞧，你会得到一个具体的数字。

sentences.en: And that number tells you just how much inflation is affecting you.
sentences.zh: 这个数字告诉你通胀对你的影响程度。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You tell us a little bit about your spending over the last year and we tell you your rate of inflation.
sentences.zh: 你告诉我们过去一年你的消费情况，我们就会告诉你你的通胀率。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So in the spirit of candor and experimentation,
sentences.zh: 那么，本着坦诚和实验的精神，

sentences.en: I'm going to fill out this inflation calculator that you all have created right here.
sentences.zh: 我要填写一下你们创建的这个通胀计算器。

sentences.en: I'm going to talk about the results.
sentences.zh: 我会谈谈结果。

sentences.en: Do it.
sentences.zh: 做吧。

sentences.en: I'll do it along with you here.
sentences.zh: 我跟你一起做。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So the first question in this calculator is, did you buy a car in the last year?
sentences.zh: 计算器的第一个问题是：你去年买车了吗？

sentences.en: And the answer is for me, yes, I bought a used car, had a kid, needed a more reliable vehicle.
sentences.zh: 我的回答是：是的，我买了一辆二手车，有了孩子，需要一辆更可靠的车。

sentences.en: So I'm going to click, I bought a used car.
sentences.zh: 所以我点击“我买了一辆二手车”。

sentences.en: I can already tell you this is going to be bad news for you.
sentences.zh: 我已经可以告诉你，这对你来说是个坏消息。

sentences.en: Because?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Car prices, pretty crazy right now.
sentences.zh: 现在的车价非常疯狂。

sentences.en: Supply chain issues, big levels of inflation.
sentences.zh: 供应链问题，高水平的通胀。

sentences.en: Lots of demand.
sentences.zh: 需求量很大。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: How much do you drive?
sentences.zh: 你开车多吗？

sentences.en: Is a dropdown menu at least 400 miles per week?
sentences.zh: 下拉菜单里有“每周至少400英里”？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: Between 150 and 400 miles per week, that's high.
sentences.zh: “每周150到400英里”，那很高了。

sentences.en: I see less than 150 miles per week.
sentences.zh: 我选“每周少于150英里”。

sentences.en: I'm going to click that.
sentences.zh: 我要点这个。

sentences.en: It's probably a little less than your, your average American.
sentences.zh: 这可能比普通美国人要少一点。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Next question.
sentences.zh: 下一个问题。

sentences.en: How much do you travel?
sentences.zh: 你旅行多吗？

sentences.en: I'm going to click.
sentences.zh: 我要点击。

sentences.en: I typically take a trip or two per year.
sentences.zh: 我通常每年旅行一两次。

sentences.en: Keep going.
sentences.zh: 继续。

sentences.en: Are you a vegetarian?
sentences.zh: 你是素食主义者吗？

sentences.en: Is the next question.
sentences.zh: 这是下一个问题。

sentences.en: I am not a vegetarian with apologies if that applies to you.
sentences.zh: 我不是素食主义者，如果这适用于你，我表示歉意。

sentences.en: Next question.
sentences.zh: 下一个问题。

sentences.en: Do you heat your home with oil?
sentences.zh: 你用油取暖吗？

sentences.en: I do heat my home with oil.
sentences.zh: 我确实用油取暖。

sentences.en: How often do you eat out?
sentences.zh: 你多久出去吃一次饭？

sentences.en: I'm clicking.
sentences.zh: 我正在点击。

sentences.en: I typically eat out one or two days a week.
sentences.zh: 我通常每周出去吃一两次。

sentences.en: Final question.
sentences.zh: 最后一个问题。

sentences.en: Do you pay for school?
sentences.zh: 你支付学费吗？

sentences.en: And I'm seeing as an option, I pay for daycare or preschool.
sentences.zh: 我看到一个选项是“我支付托儿费或学前班费用”。

sentences.en: I do pay for daycare.
sentences.zh: 我确实支付托儿费。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: I have just finished this quiz and I have gotten my inflation rate and it is high.
sentences.zh: 我刚刚完成了这个测验，得到了我的通胀率，很高。

sentences.en: My personal rate of inflation is 12.5%.
sentences.zh: 我个人的通胀率是12.5%。

sentences.en: That's a, that's a big number.
sentences.zh: 那是个很大的数字。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's a lot.
sentences.zh: 非常高。

sentences.en: Do you want to hear my inflation rate?
sentences.zh: 你想听听我的通胀率吗？

sentences.en: Uh, maybe.
sentences.zh: 呃，也许吧。

sentences.en: What is yours?
sentences.zh: 你是多少？

sentences.en: 7% Michael.
sentences.zh: 7%，迈克尔。

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: So I didn't have to buy a car, which is a big part of it.
sentences.zh: 因为我不需要买车，这是很大一部分原因。

sentences.en: And you know, what's interesting, right?
sentences.zh: 你知道，这很有趣，对吧？

sentences.en: We've got these different rates of inflation.
sentences.zh: 我们有不同的通胀率。

sentences.en: You and I are pretty similar in a lot of ways, right?
sentences.zh: 你我在很多方面都很相似，对吧？

sentences.en: We're, you know, early middle-aged white guys in the New York area.
sentences.zh: 我们是纽约地区的早期中年白人男性。

sentences.en: Uh, there are people with significantly larger differences right now, both in the rates of inflation that they're
sentences.zh: 呃，现在有人的差异要大得多，无论是在他们所经历的通胀率上，

sentences.en: experiencing and in their ability to deal with that inflation and to navigate their way through this economy right now.
sentences.zh: 还是在他们应对通胀以及在当前经济中寻找出路的能力上。

sentences.en: If you imagine people in different income brackets, in different geographies, or, you know, one way I like to think about it is in, in different stages of life.
sentences.zh: 如果你想象一下不同收入阶层、不同地理位置的人，或者，我喜欢从不同人生阶段的角度来思考。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: They're experiencing this economy in, in very different ways right now.
sentences.zh: 他们现在以非常不同的方式感受着这种经济状况。

sentences.en: Well, let's talk about stages of life and how that positions people to absorb or not absorb
sentences.zh: 好吧，让我们谈谈人生阶段，以及这如何决定了人们能否承受

sentences.en: this pretty meaningful level of inflation in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国经济中这种相当显著的通胀水平。

sentences.en: economy.
sentences.zh: 经济。

sentences.en: How do you think about that?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么看待这个问题的？

sentences.en: I kind of think about it as, as sort of three phases.
sentences.zh: 我把它看作是三个阶段。

sentences.en: There's how are young adults just getting going in their careers?
sentences.zh: 刚开始职业生涯的年轻人怎么样？

sentences.en: How are they doing there?
sentences.zh: 他们过得怎么样？

sentences.en: How are people in kind of the broadly defined middle age doing?
sentences.zh: 广义上的中年人过得怎么样？

sentences.en: Us.
sentences.zh: 我们。

sentences.en: And then there are our retirees who are having a very different experience of this economy right now.
sentences.zh: 还有我们的退休人员，他们现在对这种经济的感受截然不同。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Well, let's talk about these three categories.
sentences.zh: 好吧，让我们谈谈这三类人。

sentences.en: Let's start quite naturally, if we're dealing with a life cycle, with younger Americans.
sentences.zh: 如果我们处理的是生命周期，那么很自然地，让我们从年轻的美国人开始。

sentences.en: What is their experience of inflation and how are they positioned right now to experience inflation in this moment?
sentences.zh: 他们对通胀的体验是什么？他们目前处于什么样的位置来应对这一时刻的通胀？

sentences.en: So young people, young adults are doing pretty well right now.
sentences.zh: 年轻人，年轻成年人目前过得还不错。

sentences.en: This is a generality, right?
sentences.zh: 这是一种概括，对吧？

sentences.en: And this is going to be true across all of these age groups, right?
sentences.zh: 所有这些年龄组都是如此，对吧？

sentences.en: There are tremendous variations among different people in different circumstances.
sentences.zh: 不同的人在不同的情况下有巨大的差异。

sentences.en: There are plenty of people who are struggling in all of these groups.
sentences.zh: 在所有这些群体中，都有很多人在挣扎。

sentences.en: But young people as a whole are positioned pretty well right now.
sentences.zh: 但总体而言，年轻人目前处于相当有利的位置。

sentences.en: And that may be surprising.
sentences.zh: 这可能会让人感到惊讶。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Because a lot of the things we're talking about when we talk about inflation are hitting young people pretty hard.
sentences.zh: 因为当我们谈论通胀时，我们谈论的很多事情对年轻人打击很大。

sentences.en: Young people on average have lower incomes, right?
sentences.zh: 年轻人平均收入较低，对吧？

sentences.en: So a lot of their money goes towards things like food and gas, which are things that are rising really rapidly in price right now.
sentences.zh: 所以他们的大部分钱都花在食品和汽油等东西上，而这些东西的价格现在上涨得非常快。

sentences.en: As a percentage of their overall income.
sentences.zh: 占他们总收入的比例。

sentences.en: As a percentage of their income.
sentences.zh: 占他们收入的比例。

sentences.en: They're more likely buying used cars rather than new cars, right?
sentences.zh: 他们更有可能购买二手车而不是新车，对吧？

sentences.en: And used car prices are crazy.
sentences.zh: 而二手车价格高得离谱。

sentences.en: They tend to rent rather than own and rents are going crazy.
sentences.zh: 他们倾向于租房而不是买房，而租金也在疯狂上涨。

sentences.en: So many of them are probably dealing with faster than average inflation.
sentences.zh: 所以他们中的许多人可能正在经历高于平均水平的通胀。

sentences.en: But they are also really benefiting from the parts of this economy that are working well right now.
sentences.zh: 但他们也确实从当前运行良好的经济领域中获益良多。

sentences.en: You know, you and I have talked about this before, how there are all these job openings right now.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你我之前讨论过这个问题，现在到处都是职位空缺。

sentences.en: Employers are desperate to hire and workers are able to play employers off of one another to get better pay and better opportunities.
sentences.zh: 雇主们急于招人，而求职者则可以利用雇主之间的竞争来争取更好的薪酬和机会。

sentences.en: And young people are really the ones who are in the best position on average to take advantage of that.
sentences.zh: 而年轻人平均而言，确实处于最能利用这一优势的位置。

sentences.en: Just explain why that is.
sentences.zh: 请解释一下为什么会这样。

sentences.en: Well, so imagine a couple of young people right now, you know, maybe maybe one, a new college graduate, one who didn't go to college.
sentences.zh: 嗯，想象一下现在的几个年轻人，比如一个刚大学毕业，另一个没上过大学。

sentences.en: Both of them are probably in a position right now to really seek out those best opportunities.
sentences.zh: 他们两人现在可能都处于能够积极寻找最佳机会的位置。

sentences.en: You know that the guy who didn't go to college, maybe he's working in fast food, maybe he's working in retail, maybe he's working construction
sentences.zh: 你知道，那个没上过大学的人，可能在做快餐，可能在做零售，也可能在做建筑工作，

sentences.en: and could have easily seen pay go from $10 an hour to $12 an hour to $15 an hour.
sentences.zh: 他很容易就能看到工资从每小时10美元涨到12美元，再涨到15美元。

sentences.en: You know, we're hearing now about places paying $18 an hour for jobs that would have paid minimum wage a few years ago.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们现在听说有些地方为几年前只付最低工资的工作开出了每小时18美元的薪水。

sentences.en: And those people are in a position much more readily to go and say, hey, look, I'm working at Chipotle right now, but the Codoba down the street is paying a buck more an hour.
sentences.zh: 这些人更容易去说，嘿，看，我现在在Chipotle工作，但街对面的Codoba每小时多给一美元。

sentences.en: So I'm going to go take advantage of that.
sentences.zh: 所以我打算去利用这个机会。

sentences.en: You know, it's easy to sort of move back and forth.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这种跳槽很容易。

sentences.en: And we hear, I talk to people all the time who are doing exactly that.
sentences.zh: 我们经常听到，我一直在和做这种事的人交谈。

sentences.en: For the college graduate, right, it's probably a little bit different.
sentences.zh: 对于大学毕业生来说，情况可能有点不同。

sentences.en: It's probably a little bit less of that, like chasing, you know, a dollar more an hour.
sentences.zh: 他们可能没那么频繁地去追求每小时多赚一美元。

sentences.en: But you graduate from college right now, you can get a job.
sentences.zh: 但你现在大学毕业，就能找到工作。

sentences.en: Chances are you can get a job where you have a fair bit of flexibility around, you know, exactly the nature of that job, where you may be able to advance quickly
sentences.zh: 很有可能你找到的工作具有相当大的灵活性，而且你可能能够迅速晋升，

sentences.en: because people are moving around above you.
sentences.zh: 因为你上面的人也在不断变动。

sentences.en: And we know from economic research that entering the job market during a strong period for the economy sets you up for the future in a really important way.
sentences.zh: 我们从经济研究中得知，在经济强劲时期进入就业市场，会以非常重要的方式为你未来的发展打下基础。

sentences.en: You know, people who graduated from college in 2008, 2009, the last recession, took years to overcome that hurdle of not being able to find a decent job when they got out.
sentences.zh: 你知道，2008年、2009年上一次经济衰退期间大学毕业的人，花了多年时间才克服了毕业时找不到体面工作的障碍。

sentences.en: Young people today are graduating into an environment where they can, I don't want to say write their own ticket, but they've got a lot of opportunities.
sentences.zh: 今天的年轻人毕业于一个他们可以——我不想说“随心所欲”——但他们确实有很多机会的环境。

sentences.en: And that is really optimistic for the future.
sentences.zh: 这对未来来说确实是非常乐观的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And the thing about being young is that you can take risks with your career that older people are just
sentences.zh: 年轻的好处在于，你可以在职业生涯中承担风险，而年长的人只是

sentences.en: less inclined to take, to jump between jobs, for example, because their obligations are different.
sentences.zh: 不太愿意去冒这个险，比如频繁跳槽，因为他们的负担不同。

sentences.en: Their risk aversion is greater.
sentences.zh: 他们的风险厌恶程度更高。

sentences.en: You can take risks.
sentences.zh: 你可以承担风险。

sentences.en: You can move to where the jobs are better.
sentences.zh: 你可以搬到工作机会更好的地方去。

sentences.en: You don't need to worry about the house or the car or the kid in the same way, right?
sentences.zh: 你不需要像他们那样担心房子、车子或孩子，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, you've got that kind of flexibility that you don't have otherwise.
sentences.zh: 是的，你拥有那种别人所没有的灵活性。

sentences.en: So in general, young people are relatively, and I guess surprisingly well positioned, to absorb all this inflation we're talking about.
sentences.zh: 所以总的来说，年轻人相对而言，而且令人惊讶地处于有利地位，能够消化我们所谈论的所有通货膨胀。

sentences.en: That seems to be the big takeaway.
sentences.zh: 这似乎是最大的收获。

sentences.en: Yeah, they're the ones who are most likely to be getting the pay increases to keep up with price increases.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们最有可能获得加薪以跟上物价上涨的步伐。

sentences.en: And there's another wrinkle here.
sentences.zh: 这里还有另一个复杂因素。

sentences.en: Lots of young people have student debt.
sentences.zh: 很多年轻人有学生贷款。

sentences.en: And right now, of course, student debt is on pause.
sentences.zh: 当然，目前学生贷款处于暂停状态。

sentences.en: They're not needing to make those payments, right?
sentences.zh: 他们不需要偿还这些贷款，对吧？

sentences.en: So that's a big advantage.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个巨大的优势。

sentences.en: And even if those payments start back up again, whenever that happens, you know, those debts are in fixed dollars.
sentences.zh: 即使这些还款重新开始，无论何时发生，你知道，这些债务是固定金额的。

sentences.en: And what is inflation?
sentences.zh: 什么是通货膨胀？

sentences.en: Inflation is the value of the dollar getting smaller.
sentences.zh: 通货膨胀就是美元的价值在缩水。

sentences.en: So as we see inflation pick up and people's wages pick up to keep up with it, then those debts actually get smaller in terms of a share of young people's budgets.
sentences.zh: 因此，随着我们看到通胀上升，人们的工资也随之增加以跟上步伐，那么这些债务在年轻人预算中所占的比例实际上变小了。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So a final benefit of inflation for a young person is that in relative terms, it reduces the burden of their debts.
sentences.zh: 所以通胀对年轻人的最后一个好处是，从相对角度来看，它减轻了他们的债务负担。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So what about middle-aged Americans?
sentences.zh: 那么中年美国人呢？

sentences.en: How are they positioned to handle this moment of inflation?
sentences.zh: 他们处于什么位置来应对当前的通胀时刻？

sentences.en: And how exactly are we defining middle age?
sentences.zh: 我们到底该如何定义中年？

sentences.en: I'm defining middle age very broadly here, right?
sentences.zh: 我在这里对中年的定义非常宽泛，对吧？

sentences.en: Think about people in their, you know,
sentences.zh: 想想那些处于，你知道，

sentences.en: 30s, 40s, 50s, 50s, more likely to have kids, more likely to have mortgages, right?
sentences.zh: 30多岁、40多岁、50多岁的人，他们更有可能有孩子，更有可能有抵押贷款，对吧？

sentences.en: More likely to have all of the things that make them not as flexible as all those young people we were just talking about.
sentences.zh: 他们更有可能有所有那些让他们不像我们刚才谈到的年轻人那样灵活的东西。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so a lot of middle-aged people right now are getting squeezed.
sentences.zh: 所以很多中年人现在正感到压力重重。

sentences.en: They don't have that opportunity to move around easily between jobs.
sentences.zh: 他们没有那种在工作之间轻松转换的机会。

sentences.en: You know, you think about risk-taking in youth, right?
sentences.zh: 你知道，想想年轻时的冒险精神，对吧？

sentences.en: This is like max risk aversion moment.
sentences.zh: 现在是风险厌恶达到顶峰的时刻。

sentences.en: It's not that easy to pick up and start a new job or look for a new job when you've got the mortgage on the line, when you've got the kids you've got to be paying for.
sentences.zh: 当你背负着抵押贷款，当你需要抚养孩子时，想要辞职开始一份新工作或寻找新工作并不容易。

sentences.en: So I think they're not able to take advantage to the same degree of all the things that are good in the economy right now.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为他们无法像年轻人那样充分利用当前经济中的有利因素。

sentences.en: And they're still dealing with a lot of the stuff that is bad in the economy right now in terms of inflation.
sentences.zh: 而且他们仍然要应对当前经济中许多不利的方面，即通货膨胀。

sentences.en: Well, talk, talk through that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，详细说说这个。

sentences.en: The kind of financial life of a middle-aged American when it comes to inflation.
sentences.zh: 中年美国人在通胀背景下的财务生活。

sentences.en: Think about this as a group that is often going to have a commute.
sentences.zh: 把这看作是一个通常需要通勤的群体。

sentences.en: And so they're going to be dealing with gas prices.
sentences.zh: 所以他们必须应对汽油价格。

sentences.en: They're going to need to-
sentences.zh: 他们需要——

sentences.en: Replace a car.
sentences.zh: 换车。

sentences.en: Replace the car.
sentences.zh: 换车。

sentences.en: And look, if you've got kids really thinking about the safety of the car, and so you don't want to drive that junker around, right?
sentences.zh: 而且看，如果你有孩子，真的会考虑车的安全性，所以你不想开那辆破车，对吧？

sentences.en: Childcare.
sentences.zh: 托儿服务。

sentences.en: Childcare is a huge expense.
sentences.zh: 托儿服务是一笔巨大的开支。

sentences.en: Food, right?
sentences.zh: 食物，对吧？

sentences.en: If you've got kids again, right, is going to be a huge expense.
sentences.zh: 如果你有孩子，这又是一笔巨大的开支。

sentences.en: They're dealing with all of the things that are getting more expensive in life without having the same ability to go and hunt down the better pay, better options that young
sentences.zh: 他们正在应对生活中所有变得越来越昂贵的东西，却没有年轻人那样去追求更高薪水和更好选择的能力，

sentences.en: people may be able to go and chase right now.
sentences.zh: 年轻人现在可能能够去追求这些。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Thus the squeeze.
sentences.zh: 这就是压力所在。

sentences.en: Less opportunity for wage growth and a greater likelihood of being hit by all these inflationary categories.
sentences.zh: 工资增长的机会更少，而且更有可能受到所有这些通胀类别的冲击。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: There is one big caveat to this, which is housing.
sentences.zh: 对此有一个很大的警告，那就是住房。

sentences.en: You know, people in sort of the broadly defined middle of life are more likely to own their own homes.
sentences.zh: 你知道，处于广义中年阶段的人更有可能拥有自己的住房。

sentences.en: Well, if you own your home and you've got a fixed rate mortgage, right, home prices can go crazy.
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果你拥有自己的房子并且有固定利率抵押贷款，那么房价再怎么疯狂，

sentences.en: It doesn't matter to you.
sentences.zh: 对你来说都没关系。

sentences.en: Your costs don't go up.
sentences.zh: 你的成本不会增加。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You're locked into a monthly cost that will not change in most cases for 30 years.
sentences.zh: 你被锁定在一个在大多数情况下30年内都不会改变的月供成本中。

sentences.en: And I guess like student debt in a moment of inflation, this kind of debt becomes a smaller overall share of your budget.
sentences.zh: 我想就像通胀时刻的学生贷款一样，这种债务在你预算中所占的总体比例会变小。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And in fact, if you've refinanced in the last couple of years, as millions and millions
sentences.zh: 事实上，如果你在过去几年里进行了再融资，就像数百万美国人所做的那样，

sentences.en: of Americans have, you may be paying less for housing now than you were a couple of years ago.
sentences.zh: 你现在的住房支出可能比几年前还要少。

sentences.en: So homeownership is a meaningful way to escape a significant part of inflation.
sentences.zh: 所以拥有住房是逃避很大一部分通胀的有意义的方式。

sentences.en: It has been recently.
sentences.zh: 最近确实如此。

sentences.en: Now, how many Americans and how many middle aged Americans do we estimate are homeowners?
sentences.zh: 那么，我们估计有多少美国人，有多少中年美国人是房主？

sentences.en: Well, so a majority of Americans own their homes and that's a substantial majority in that middle aged bracket.
sentences.zh: 嗯，大多数美国人拥有自己的住房，而在中年群体中，这一比例占绝大多数。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So this is going to be a lot of people are going to have that advantage, even as they're getting squeezed in all these other ways.
sentences.zh: 所以很多人都会拥有这种优势，即使他们在其他方面感到压力。

sentences.en: This also highlights how these experiences can be very different for different people.
sentences.zh: 这也凸显了这些经历对不同的人来说可能非常不同。

sentences.en: If you've got all those things, you've got the kid and you've got the car and you've got the food and you've got the gas, but you're renting and you're dealing with the
sentences.zh: 如果你有所有这些负担，有孩子、有车、有食物开销、有汽油费，但你是在租房，而且你正在应对

sentences.en: rising price of cost of rent right now in many cities, then you are really getting squeezed.
sentences.zh: 许多城市目前不断上涨的房租，那么你真的会感到压力巨大。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So the story of middle aged Americans is.
sentences.zh: 所以中年美国人的故事是。

sentences.en: Much like middle aged itself.
sentences.zh: 就像中年本身一样。

sentences.en: A little bit of a bummer.
sentences.zh: 有点令人沮丧。

sentences.en: I think that's true for a lot of people right now.
sentences.zh: 我认为这对很多人来说现在都是事实。

sentences.en: And we haven't even gotten to what it's like to try to live in retirement right now.
sentences.zh: 而且我们甚至还没谈到目前退休生活是什么样的。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app unlocked.
sentences.zh: 解锁《纽约时报》应用程序。

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道你需要订阅《时报》才能访问所有的报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month for free without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果你能免费试用《时报》一个月而无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在应用里的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间越过付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用程序，获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: So, Ben, let's talk about what inflation is like for retired Americans.
sentences.zh: 那么，本，我们来谈谈退休美国人的通胀情况。

sentences.en: What do we need to know?
sentences.zh: 我们需要了解什么？

sentences.en: Well, so all that stuff we talked about, about the good job market and lots of job openings and playing employers off each other, by definition, none of that is relevant here.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们刚才谈到的所有关于良好的就业市场、大量的职位空缺以及雇主之间的竞争，根据定义，这些在这里都不适用。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You're out of the job market.
sentences.zh: 你已经退出了就业市场。

sentences.en: You're out of the job market.
sentences.zh: 你已经退出了就业市场。

sentences.en: So retirees are not benefiting from those pieces of the economy that are working really well for them.
sentences.zh: 所以退休人员并没有从那些对他们运行良好的经济部分中受益。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I tend to think of retired workers as, in general, not being especially well-positioned
sentences.zh: 我倾向于认为退休人员总体上并不是特别处于有利地位，

sentences.en: to handle something like inflation because of all the things in their lives that are inflexible,
sentences.zh: 来应对像通胀这样的事情，因为他们生活中所有不灵活的地方，

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, that's right.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，没错。

sentences.en: Retirees, in many cases, are living on a fixed income, right?
sentences.zh: 退休人员在许多情况下靠固定收入生活，对吧？

sentences.en: The money that's coming in every month is what it is, or they're drawing down retirement accounts.
sentences.zh: 每个月进账的钱就是那么多，或者他们正在动用退休账户。

sentences.en: Or drawing down savings.
sentences.zh: 或者动用储蓄。

sentences.en: Or drawing down savings.
sentences.zh: 或者动用储蓄。

sentences.en: And they're dealing with all the costs of living.
sentences.zh: 而且他们要应对所有的生活成本。

sentences.en: And so there's often very little flexibility in that budget.
sentences.zh: 所以预算中通常几乎没有灵活性。

sentences.en: And we know that retirees, in particular, tend to be really worried about inflation.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，退休人员尤其担心通货膨胀。

sentences.en: We see that in survey data.
sentences.zh: 我们在调查数据中看到了这一点。

sentences.en: I certainly hear that when
sentences.zh: 当我与人交谈时，

sentences.en: I'm talking to people.
sentences.zh: 我肯定会听到这些。

sentences.en: That said, it's a little bit more of a complicated picture than you might initially think.
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，情况比你最初想象的要复杂一些。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Well, so, for one thing, on the cost side of the equation, retirees are very often going to be homeowners.
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先，在成本方面，退休人员通常是房主。

sentences.en: They are often going to be driving less, right?
sentences.zh: 他们通常开车较少，对吧？

sentences.en: We don't have that commute problem, right?
sentences.zh: 我们没有那个通勤问题，对吧？

sentences.en: They may be spending less of their budget on some of those things where we're really seeing a lot of cost increases right now.
sentences.zh: 他们可能在预算中花费较少的部分用于那些我们现在确实看到成本大幅增加的项目。

sentences.en: And although we talk about retirees as living on a fixed income, that's not always the case.
sentences.zh: 虽然我们说退休人员靠固定收入生活，但这并不总是事实。

sentences.en: Social Security, in particular, is indexed to inflation.
sentences.zh: 社会保障金尤其与通胀挂钩。

sentences.en: Explain that.
sentences.zh: 解释一下。

sentences.en: So, the Social Security check that you get every month, once a year, gets adjusted based on cost of living, based on the consumer price index.
sentences.zh: 所以，你每个月收到的社会保障支票，每年会根据生活成本，根据消费者价格指数进行一次调整。

sentences.en: And earlier this year, retirees, Social
sentences.zh: 今年早些时候，退休人员，即社会保障金领取者，获得了他们

sentences.en: Security recipients, got the biggest increase in their monthly checks that they've gotten in
sentences.zh: 40年来月度支票中最大的涨幅。

sentences.en: 40 years.
A 5.9% increase.
Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And assuming that we continue to see the kind of inflation that we've seen, next year, they will get another increase.
sentences.zh: 如果假设我们继续看到目前这种通胀水平，明年他们还会再涨一次。

sentences.en: So, the government understanding that retired Americans are on something like a fixed income literally boosts the payments it's giving to tens of millions of retired workers.
sentences.zh: 所以，政府明白退休的美国人靠的是固定收入，因此确实提高了发放给数千万退休工人的补助金。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Now, look, this is every year, not every month.
sentences.zh: 但你要知道，这是按年计算的，不是按月。

sentences.en: And so, you know, when gas prices spike the way they have recently, it's not like everybody's check suddenly gets bigger as a result.
sentences.zh: 所以，当汽油价格像最近这样飙升时，并不是说每个人的支票都会因此突然变大。

sentences.en: And retirees obviously don't have the ability to go to their employer and say, come on, you've seen what's going on with gas prices, you've got to give me a raise.
sentences.zh: 而且退休人员显然没有能力去找雇主说：拜托，你看到油价涨成什么样了，你得给我涨工资。

sentences.en: So, I don't want to overstate the degree to which they're insulated from this.
sentences.zh: 所以，我不想夸大他们能在多大程度上免受这种影响。

sentences.en: To be clear, many retirees are absolutely getting squeezed by rising prices and a limited ability to increase their income.
sentences.zh: 说清楚点，许多退休人员绝对正受到物价上涨和收入增长能力有限的双重挤压。

sentences.en: But when we look sort of across broad averages, retirees are often, in many cases, going to be in a better position than some of those middle-aged people
sentences.zh: 但当我们从广泛的平均水平来看时，退休人员在很多情况下，往往比我们之前谈到的那些中年人处境要好一些。

sentences.en: that we were talking about earlier.
sentences.zh: 我们之前谈到的那些人。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Or the popular imagination of the retired worker who's kind of stuck.
sentences.zh: 或者说，大众印象中那种陷入困境的退休工人。

sentences.en: We have this idea of, like, retirees, there's nothing they can do.
sentences.zh: 我们有一种观念，觉得退休人员好像什么都做不了。

sentences.en: And it's not always quite as simple as that.
sentences.zh: 但事实并非总是那么简单。

sentences.en: So, Ben, now that we've surveyed the impacts of inflation across these various age brackets, what's clear is that the impact of inflation is very broadly felt.
sentences.zh: 所以，本，既然我们已经调查了通胀对各个年龄段的影响，显而易见的是，通胀的影响是非常广泛的。

sentences.en: I mean, depending on your age, you're going to experience it differently, but it's hurting almost everyone.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，根据年龄不同，你的感受会有所差异，但它几乎伤害了每一个人。

sentences.en: And so, to return to the inflation calculator for a moment where we started this conversation, that makes
sentences.zh: 所以，回到我们谈话开始时的那个通胀计算器，这让我

sentences.en: me wonder if there are ways for people to lower their personal inflation costs.
sentences.zh: 想知道人们是否有办法降低个人的通胀成本。

sentences.en: It seems like a natural place to start would be with the categories that you identified as the biggest sources of inflation.
sentences.zh: 一个自然的切入点似乎应该是你确定的那些通胀的主要来源。

sentences.en: You know, your car, your driving, your meat consumption.
sentences.zh: 比如，你的车、你的驾驶习惯、你的肉类消费。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: I mean, it's really tempting.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这真的很诱人。

sentences.en: You know, you look at this inflation calculator and you say, oh, cars are way up.
sentences.zh: 你知道，看着这个通胀计算器，你会说，哦，汽车价格涨得太高了。

sentences.en: So, you know, try not to buy a car.
sentences.zh: 所以，尽量别买车。

sentences.en: And, you know, it looks like it's cheaper to be a vegetarian.
sentences.zh: 而且，看起来吃素更便宜。

sentences.en: I'll drop meat.
sentences.zh: 那我就不吃肉了。

sentences.en: It's not really that simple for a couple of reasons.
sentences.zh: 但由于几个原因，这其实没那么简单。

sentences.en: The first is that a lot of the things that have been rising most quickly in price recently are things where it's pretty hard to cut back.
sentences.zh: 首先，最近价格上涨最快的东西，很多都是很难削减开支的。

sentences.en: Maybe you can find some ways to drive a little bit less to, you know, combine some trips together, right?
sentences.zh: 也许你可以想办法少开点车，比如把几次行程合并在一起，对吧？

sentences.en: But if you've got a daily commute, you've got a daily commute.
sentences.zh: 但如果你每天都要通勤，那就必须得通勤。

sentences.en: The grocery store is 10 miles away.
sentences.zh: 杂货店在10英里外。

sentences.en: It's 10 miles away, right?
sentences.zh: 它就是10英里远，对吧？

sentences.en: What are you going to do about this?
sentences.zh: 你对此能做什么呢？

sentences.en: You can't cut back and say we're not going to eat this week.
sentences.zh: 你不能削减开支说这周我们不吃饭了。

sentences.en: Also, the things that have risen the most in price over the last year are not necessarily the things that are going to rise the most in price over the next year.
sentences.zh: 此外，过去一年价格涨幅最大的东西，不一定就是明年价格涨幅最大的东西。

sentences.en: We've actually seen used car prices have started to edge down a little bit recently.
sentences.zh: 我们实际上已经看到二手车价格最近开始略有回落。

sentences.en: Oil prices, you know, been up and down, but we can all hope that if things kind of calm down in the world, that oil prices will start to come down.
sentences.zh: 油价呢，起起伏伏，但我们都可以希望，如果世界局势平稳下来，油价会开始下降。

sentences.en: So you can end up in this place where you sort of are constantly fighting the last war and trying to adjust your spending to account for things that have already happened.
sentences.zh: 所以你最终可能会陷入这种境地：你一直在打上一场战争，试图调整你的支出以应对已经发生的事情。

sentences.en: Trying to target your inflation rate is probably not a realistic way to live your life.
sentences.zh: 试图针对你的通胀率来生活，可能并不是一种现实的生活方式。

sentences.en: So what is the best way at a moment when, whether it's 7% or 12.5%, our lives are just getting that much more expensive that you can cut costs if
sentences.zh: 那么，当我们的生活成本变得如此昂贵时，无论是7%还是12.5%，如果

sentences.en: you're not recommending here, going after the most identifiable sources of inflation?
sentences.zh: 你不建议去针对那些最明显的通胀来源，那最好的削减成本的方法是什么？

sentences.en: Well, so my best advice is the thing that I think a lot of people are probably already doing, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我最好的建议是很多人可能已经在做的事情，对吧？

sentences.en: Which is that when the cost of living goes up, they find places that they can cut back in
sentences.zh: 那就是当生活成本上升时，他们会寻找可以在预算中削减的地方，

sentences.en: the budget, even if it's not necessarily cutting back on things where prices are going up really rapidly.
sentences.zh: 即使这不一定是在那些价格飞涨的项目上削减开支。

sentences.en: You know, clothes prices have not been on fire recently.
sentences.zh: 你知道，服装价格最近并没有疯涨。

sentences.en: But, you know, maybe you can cut back your clothes spending a little bit and save a little bit of money in the budget.
sentences.zh: 但是，也许你可以稍微减少一点服装支出，在预算中省下一小笔钱。

sentences.en: And I think this highlights something really important about inflation, which is that totally aside from
sentences.zh: 我认为这突显了关于通胀的一个非常重要的问题，那就是完全撇开

sentences.en: whether you're experiencing a fast inflation rate or a slow inflation rate, inflation really hurts people the most when they don't have that kind of flexibility in their budgets.
sentences.zh: 你经历的是高通胀率还是低通胀率，当人们预算中没有那种灵活性时，通胀对他们的伤害最大。

sentences.en: Somebody can't say,
sentences.zh: 有人不能说，

sentences.en: I'm not going to buy milk for my kid this week.
sentences.zh: 我这周不给孩子买牛奶了。

sentences.en: You know, I'm not going to pay the electrical bill this month.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我这个月不交电费了。

sentences.en: If you're already buying the off-brand laundry detergent, you can't cut back to that.
sentences.zh: 如果你已经在买非品牌的洗衣液了，你就没法再削减了。

sentences.en: And so there are a lot fewer options to cut back on your spending when you're poorer.
sentences.zh: 所以当你更贫穷时，削减支出的选择就少得多。

sentences.en: And that's why inflation is such a problem for poorer households.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么通胀对贫困家庭来说是个大问题。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Because it means the baseline, that which was supposed to be reliably affordable, is just that much less affordable.
sentences.zh: 因为它意味着基准线，那些本应是可靠且负担得起的东西，变得更难以负担了。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And a lot of the things that are rising rapidly in price right now are things that it's just very hard to avoid.
sentences.zh: 而且现在价格飞涨的很多东西，都是很难避免的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, quite literally, the pillars of our lives, gas, food, car.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，从字面上看，是我们生活的支柱：汽油、食物、汽车。

sentences.en: And if you're a renter, rent.
sentences.zh: 如果你是租房者，那就是房租。

sentences.en: So, Ben, how long, and I know you don't like predictions, so based this on your reporting
sentences.zh: 所以，本，我们要多久，我知道你不喜欢预测，所以根据你的报道

sentences.en: and the data you spend time with, how long are we going to be in this inflationary universe that
sentences.zh: 和你花时间研究的数据，我们还要在这个我们一直在谈论的通胀世界里待多久，

sentences.en: we have been talking about where so many people need to make these cutbacks to absorb these higher costs?
sentences.zh: 在这个世界里，这么多人需要做出这些削减来消化这些更高的成本？

sentences.en: Are we looking at a year, two years, six months, five years?
sentences.zh: 我们面对的是一年、两年、六个月，还是五年？

sentences.en: You know, they told me I couldn't come in the studio unless I promise not to say time will tell.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们告诉我，除非我保证不说“时间会证明一切”，否则就不让我进演播室。

sentences.en: So I won't say that.
sentences.zh: 所以我不会那么说。

sentences.en: The guards explicitly warned you.
sentences.zh: 警卫明确警告过你。

sentences.en: What I'll say is this.
sentences.zh: 我想说的是这个。

sentences.en: We know that Russia's invasion of Ukraine has driven up gas prices.
sentences.zh: 我们知道俄罗斯入侵乌克兰推高了汽油价格。

sentences.en: We know that the pandemic is still going, and in particular, having a big effect in China,
sentences.zh: 我们知道疫情仍在持续，特别是在中国产生了巨大影响，

sentences.en: leading to lockdowns, exacerbating all the supply chain issues that we've all been talking about.
sentences.zh: 导致封锁，加剧了我们一直在谈论的所有供应链问题。

sentences.en: Right, and leading to higher prices among all the products we get from China.
sentences.zh: 没错，并导致我们从中国进口的所有产品价格上涨。

sentences.en: We know we're still dealing with this really tight labor market and the wages that come with it, right?
sentences.zh: 我们知道我们仍在应对这个非常紧张的劳动力市场以及随之而来的工资问题，对吧？

sentences.en: So we know that these forces are still in place.
sentences.zh: 所以我们知道这些力量依然存在。

sentences.en: We know that the Federal Reserve is trying very hard to fight inflation by raising interest rates, but that none of that is going to have an overnight impact.
sentences.zh: 我们知道美联储正在通过提高利率努力对抗通胀，但这些都不会产生立竿见影的影响。

sentences.en: And what that means is that whether you're a young person trying to take advantage of this strong job market, but dealing with rising rents, or you're a middle-aged person,
sentences.zh: 这意味着，无论你是试图利用这个强劲就业市场但又要应对房租上涨的年轻人，还是一个中年人，

sentences.en: dealing with all of the costs of life, or a retiree kind of looking at that retirement count and getting nervous, right?
sentences.zh: 要应对生活中的所有成本，或者是一个看着退休账户感到紧张的退休人员，对吧？

sentences.en: All of these people are going to have to deal with the reality of higher prices and adjust their lives accordingly.
sentences.zh: 所有这些人将不得不面对物价上涨的现实，并相应地调整他们的生活。

sentences.en: For quite some time.
sentences.zh: 在相当长的一段时间内。

sentences.en: For quite some time.
sentences.zh: 在相当长的一段时间内。

sentences.en: Ben, as always, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 本，一如既往，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你邀请我。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的其他消息。

sentences.en: Now, Madam President, the question before the Senate is simple.
sentences.zh: 现在，议长女士，参议院面前的问题很简单。

sentences.en: As women's rights face their greatest threat in half a century, will this chamber step into the breach and protect the basic right to choose?
sentences.zh: 当女性权利面临半个世纪以来最大的威胁时，这个议院会挺身而出，保护基本的选择权吗？

sentences.en: On Wednesday, Senate Democrats tried and failed to pass legislation that would guarantee the right
sentences.zh: 周三，参议院民主党人试图通过一项旨在保障堕胎权的立法，但以失败告终，

sentences.en: to an abortion, seeking to enshrine in federal law what they fear will soon be struck down by the
sentences.zh: 他们试图将他们担心很快会被最高法院推翻的权利写入联邦法律。

sentences.en: Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 最高法院。

sentences.en: But the bill, which would outlaw any limitation on abortion before fetal viability, failed to win even a simple majority.
sentences.zh: 但是这项法案，即禁止在胎儿存活能力之前对堕胎进行任何限制，甚至没能获得简单多数票。

sentences.en: It was opposed by Democratic Senator Joe Manchin and all 50 Senate
sentences.zh: 它遭到了民主党参议员乔·曼钦和所有50名参议院

sentences.en: Republicans, who called it overly permissive and extreme.
sentences.zh: 共和党人的反对，他们称其过于宽容和极端。

sentences.en: There was a time when the Democratic Party talked about abortion as safe, legal, and rare.
sentences.zh: 曾几何时，民主党谈论堕胎时称其为安全、合法且罕见。

sentences.en: Safe, legal, and rare.
sentences.zh: 安全、合法且罕见。

sentences.en: Not anymore.
sentences.zh: 现在不再是了。

sentences.en: This legislation is not from your mom's Democratic Party.
sentences.zh: 这项立法不是你母亲那个时代的民主党提出的。

sentences.en: And the families of the 98 people killed last year when a condominium tower collapsed in Surfside,
sentences.zh: 去年在佛罗里达州瑟夫赛德一栋公寓大楼倒塌中丧生的98人的家属，

sentences.en: Florida, have reached a nearly $1 billion financial settlement.
sentences.zh: 已经达成了一项近10亿美元的财务和解协议。

sentences.en: The money will be paid by a long list of defendants, including insurance companies, developers, and engineers, some of whom discovered serious structural problems in the tower
sentences.zh: 这笔钱将由一长串被告支付，包括保险公司、开发商和工程师，其中一些人在大楼倒塌前

sentences.en: before its collapse.
sentences.zh: 就发现了严重的结构性问题。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Stella Tan, Rochelle Bonja, and Mooj Zadie.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由斯特拉·谭、罗谢尔·邦贾和穆吉·扎迪制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by John Ketchum, contains original music by Marian Lozano, Dan Powell, and Rowan Nemisto, and was engineered by Chris Wood.
sentences.zh: 由约翰·凯彻姆剪辑，包含玛丽安·洛萨诺、丹·鲍威尔和罗文·内米斯托的原创音乐，并由克里斯·伍德进行工程处理。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Landfork of Wonderland.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由仙境的吉姆·布伦伯格和本·兰福克创作。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受到严格控制的机器运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 选举迎来了一批自称改革者的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直处于一场伤痕累累、混乱不堪，有时又令人兴奋的斗争之中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在《地铁》的最新一集中，我和莎拉·凯尼格一起，讲述了人们试图维持影响力却在过程中失去控制的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《地铁》。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 在任何你收听播客的地方收听。
